name: Library Science
title: Library and Information Science
intro: The library science roadmap: bachelor’s degree, B.Lib.I.Sc, M.Lib.I.Sc, UGC NET and library jobs.
glance: B.Lib.I.Sc (1 year) after a bachelor’s degree

phases.title: Class 12 and bachelor’s degree
phases.summary: Any stream; complete a bachelor’s degree first.
points: Library science is a postgraduate-level professional course in most places, so first complete a bachelor’s degree in any subject.
Reading habits and organisation skills help.
Choose a degree whose subject may help in specialised libraries (science, law, medicine).
Some universities offer integrated programmes or diplomas.

phases.title: B.Lib.I.Sc admission
points: Apply to universities through merit or entrance tests (e.g., IGNOU, state universities).
Minimum marks of 45–50% in your bachelor’s degree are typically needed.
Choose between regular and distance mode, subject to recognition.
Complete admission and fee payment.

phases.title: B.Lib.I.Sc coursework
phases.summary: Library classification, cataloguing and information services.
points: Study Library, Information and Society, Classification and Cataloguing (DDC, CC), Reference and Information Services, and Library Management.
Learn library automation and digital library software such as Koha.
Complete practicals in classification, cataloguing and reference work.
Do a project or internship in a library.

phases.title: M.Lib.I.Sc and higher study
phases.summary: One-year master’s, then NET or PhD.
points: M.Lib.I.Sc deepens the subject: research methods, information retrieval, knowledge management and bibliometrics.
UGC NET (Library and Information Science) leads to teaching and research roles.
PhD options open at universities and research institutes.
Add certificates in digital archiving, data management and open-source software.

phases.title: Careers
phases.summary: Libraries in schools, universities, institutes and companies.
points: Jobs: school librarian, college and university librarian, public library, corporate and special libraries, and digital archives.
Government: KVS/NVS librarian, state public libraries and central libraries through recruitment exams.
Related roles: information scientist, data curator, records manager.
Library jobs value digital skills and information management.
